title: Notify and Delegate: Customer Communication Playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook that combines concise status page copy, an operator handoff checklist, and a customer-facing post-incident summary template. The goal is to make notifications fast and consistent while enabling the on-call/operator to delegate customer follow-ups to CS/AE/SE teams with minimal friction.

Audience:
- Primary: Customer Success reps (CS), Account Execs (AE), Solutions Eng (SE) who may need to notify or support customers.
- Secondary: SRE/Serving Runtime on-call for technical accuracy.

High-level approach (notify + delegate):
1) Notify: publish a brief status update on Status Page and send Tiered notices for affected enterprise tenants. Keep copy short, actionable, and non-speculative.
2) Delegate: if customers require account-level communication, CS/AE receives a short handoff note from SRE including impact, expected remediation, and suggested language.
3) Follow-up: Produce a customer-facing postmortem summary within 72 hours (initial summary) and a final customer summary within 7–14 days depending on investigation progress.

Decision tree / triggers (quick):
- If >1% global latency increase OR >1 enterprise tenant degraded -> send Tier-2 (enterprise) notify and open AE channel.
- If errors or data integrity concerns -> escalate to legal/compliance immediately and draft customer notice before public postmortem.
- If streaming session truncation or structured output loss for tenants -> include example evidence and recommended mitigations in handoff.

Operator handoff checklist (copyable snippet to paste into CS Slack channel or AE email):
- Incident ID: RLW-3421
- Short summary (1 line): Intermittent model routing failures caused elevated latency and partial truncation of streaming responses for EU region.
- Impacted scope: Estimated ~4% of requests in eu-west-1 between 2026-06-09T01:12Z and 2026-06-09T02:08Z; affecting hosted API and some Dedicated routes. Specific enterprise tenants: tenant-a, tenant-b (private notes attached).
- Current status: Mitigated (redundant routing engaged, monitoring).
- Customer action recommended: None required for most customers; enterprise tenants offered forced fallback to pinned model variant on request.
- Technical lead: Amit Rao (SRE)
- Next update ETA: 30 min / 1 hour / 3 hours (pick depending on severity)
- Evidence bundle link: https://redwood-confluence/internal/incidents/rlw-3421/evidence

Status page templates (short, non-technical; choose appropriate phase):
- Identified (short): "We are investigating elevated latency and occasional truncated streaming responses affecting customers in EU regions. Customers may experience slower token delivery or incomplete structured outputs. We will share updates every 30 minutes."

- Mitigating (short): "We have activated additional routing and a fallback policy for affected requests. Most traffic is restored; some customers may still observe slower responses. Engineers continue to monitor and validate output integrity."

- Monitoring (short): "Traffic is stable and degrades have subsided. We are monitoring systems closely and continuing validation of outputs. If you see issues, please contact support with request ids and timestamps."

- Resolved (short): "The root cause has been addressed and we consider the incident resolved. If you continue to see problems, open a support ticket and include timestamps and example responses."

Customer-facing postmortem summary template (first-pass, ~72h):
[Header]
- Incident ID: RLW-3421
- Date/time window: 2026-06-09T01:12Z - 2026-06-09T02:08Z (identified)
- Affected customers: Select EU-hosted API customers and a small number of Dedicated routes (approx. 4% of requests)

[Executive summary — one paragraph, non-technical]
On 2026-06-09 we experienced an intermittent routing issue in the EU region that increased latency and caused occasional truncated streaming responses for a subset of requests. We deployed a mitigation (redundant routing + forced fallback to a pinned model variant) which restored normal service. No customer data was lost.

[What happened — technical summary for customers]
A sudden mismatch between model variant compatibility metadata and the routing policy caused a small percentage of requests to be routed to a node that could not serve the expected quantization/profile for long-running streams. That mismatch caused elevated token-latency and, in some cases, truncated structured outputs.

[Impact]
- Duration: ~56 minutes from first detection to mitigation activation.
- Scope: ~4% of requests in eu-west-1; estimated 12 enterprise accounts saw visible degradation.
- Data integrity: No evidence of data corruption or loss.

[Mitigation and remediation]
- Immediate: Engaged redundant routing and forced fallback to verified model variants for EU region.
- Follow-up fixes: Verify router metadata validation at admission time; add automated canary checks for model variant compatibility; improve streaming retry behavior to hide transient truncation.
- ETA for code rollout: low-latency router validation patch targeted in next 3 business days; automated canaries within 2 weeks.

[Customer options and next steps]
- If your application experienced truncation, you can request a temporary pin to the stable model variant via your AE; we will prioritize tenant pins where there is confirmed impact.
- For enterprise customers who require a formal evidence package for audits, contact cs-incident-pack@redwood.ai and include Incident ID RLW-3421.

[Contact and escalation]
- Primary CS contact: Claire Jensen (claire@redwood.ai)
- SRE technical lead: Amit Rao (amit@redwood.ai)
- For urgent escalations: AE on-call (see internal roster)

Open questions / items for legal & PR review:
- Draft short customer FAQ (2–3 Qs) about retries and token billing during incidents — confirm billing stance.
- Confirm wording around "no customer data loss" with Legal to ensure language satisfies regulators in EEA.

Quality checklist before publishing final customer summary:
- [ ] Confirm timeline with SRE (timestamps + correlating logs)
- [ ] Get Legal sign-off on any statements about data or billing
- [ ] AE/CS review for tone and account-specific notes
- [ ] Attach evidence bundle for enterprise customers

Examples: customer email snippet (AE friendly)
Subject: Update on recent EU inference disruption (Incident RLW-3421)
Hi <Name>,
We wanted to let you know about an incident earlier today that may have affected requests from EU regions. Briefly: there was a transient routing mismatch which has been mitigated and service is restored. If you saw truncated streaming responses, we can pin your tenant to the stable variant as a short-term measure — reply to this email or open a ticket and we’ll prioritize.
Thanks,
Claire (on behalf of SRE & CS)

Backlog / follow-ups (internal):
- Add explicit model-compatibility admission checks to routing service (RLW-3489).
- Add tenant-level incident telemetry to share with AE/CS automatically.
- Review billing implications for truncated responses and decide policy.

Notes to self (working):
- Keep Status Page updates minimal but empathetic. Customers hate uncertain technical detail — give them what they need to act.
- If Legal asks for conservative language, favor "no evidence of data loss" until logs are fully validated.
- Test the handoff snippet in next drill to measure time between detection and AE notification.

History / revision log:
- 2026-06-09 created by Claire Jensen (initial draft)
- 2026-06-11 updated by Amit Rao (added technical notes and evidence link)

End of doc.
